comments.summary: Landing pages show both cards, but the advisory repair path and target-equivalent proof path must be visually and behaviorally distinct.
No main blocker was identified for the 1.1.1 short check, but it should not be approved while the overall check system is below product standard.
The 1.1.1 exit ticket remains a candidate only; next review must judge target-equivalent quality, not only rendered existence.
The 1.1.2 short check must not weaken or duplicate the reviewed 1.1.2 exit-ticket authority.
Preserve the prior 1.1.2 reviewed authority; it remains the only locally approved completion-language case.
The 1.1.3 short check has no graph, no table/source context, no task shell, and no graph workspace.
The 1.1.3 exit-ticket data has graph-task structure, but the generated surface does not yet render as a polished source/task graph workspace.
Source/context label hygiene is useful and should remain validated, but it is not enough to prove visual QA.
Screenshots and proof JSON verify generated surfaces, but do not prove product quality or a strong playable review surface.
Authority boundaries are acceptable; the problem is insufficient product quality, not overclaim.
A single patch is not enough; the review requires a reset and product-quality sprint sequence before retrying the human gate.

blocking_findings: 1.1.3-exit data has graph task structure but generated product lacks polished source/task graph workspace
visual QA and lead review overfocused on existence, screenshots, flags, and label hygiene
